description: Indiana’s earned income credit is claimed on a state tax return. Check federal EITC eligibility and use Indiana’s forms for the year you are filing.
introduction: Indiana’s earned income credit is claimed on a state tax return. Check federal EITC eligibility and use Indiana’s forms for the year you are filing.

sections.who: Indiana’s Department of Revenue says people eligible for the federal earned income credit may qualify for the state credit. The detailed Schedule IN-EIC and IT-40 or IT-40PNR instructions determine the state claim.
sections.get: The credit is calculated through the tax filing process. Do not treat a rough online estimate as the amount due on your return.
sections.docs:
• Federal return and earned income credit calculation.
  • Income statements and relevant business records.
  • Dependent and taxpayer identification information.
  • The Indiana return and IN-EIC for the correct tax year.
sections.apply:
1. Complete the federal calculation

    Check the federal EITC rules for your filing year.

  2. Calculate the state credit

    Use Schedule IN-EIC and the applicable Indiana return instructions.

  3. File the required schedules

    DOR identifies Schedule 5 for resident returns and Schedule F for the relevant nonresident return credits. Use the return booklet to confirm attachments.
sections.after: Keep the calculation and supporting records. Read any revenue-agency request before submitting an amendment or a second claim.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using Indiana credit requirements and schedules, 2025 individual forms. The provider makes eligibility decisions.

faqs: Do I use Schedule 6 for this credit?
DOR’s credit page identifies Schedule IN-EIC with Schedule 5 or Schedule F. Follow your return’s instructions.
Which version of IN-EIC should I use?
Use the version for the tax year being claimed; the current forms page lists 2025 forms.
Yes. DOR ties the Indiana credit to federal earned income credit eligibility.
Where can I find the calculation instructions?
Use the IT-40 or IT-40PNR booklet linked from DOR’s tax forms pages.
